exposure: Schmallenberg virus (SBV) infection at 45 days of gestation
Schmallenberg virus (SBV) infection at 60 days of gestation
outcome: SBV RNA detection in lamb organs
SBV RNA detection in extraembryonic structures
frequency of detecting virus in offspring extraembryonic structures
cohort: Twenty-three Mourerous breed ewes were randomly separated into three groups: eight and nine ewes were infected with SBV at 45 and 60 days of gestation, respectively, and six control ewes were given phosphate buffer saline.
finding: Schmallenberg virus (SBV) readily colonized the placenta when ewes were infected at 45 or 60 days of gestation, but fetal infection was limited and did not lead to congenital malformations in the lambs.
gest_age: Ewes were infected at 45 or 60 days of gestation; lambs were born at term.
